messages:
alex: Heads-up — since 11:10 UTC we've seen sustained queue growth in shared-pool us-west GPU cluster. 95th tail for gen requests climbed from 120ms -> 1.6s. Looks correlated with a single heavy tenant doing long-context batched jobs.

maria: ugh. which tenant id? can we confirm it's not a network flake?

alex: tenant=acme-ads, pattern: large batch size + long seq len (>=8k). Prom metric: 
```
sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{pool="shared-us-west",job="serving"}[1m])) by (le)
```
shows backlog increase since ~11:08. Pod CPU & GPU util hit steady 98% on 3 nodes.

chen: @alex can you dump the per-tenant queue depth? I want to see how much of the queue acme-ads is occupying vs rest.

alex: pasted small snippet: 
```
tenant_queue_depth{tenant="acme-ads",pool="shared-us-west"} 142
tenant_queue_depth{tenant="small-saas",pool="shared-us-west"} 7
tenant_queue_depth{tenant="analytics-x",pool="shared-us-west"} 12
```
so acme-ads is ~90% of backlog.

leo: can we soft-preempt or move their requests to a degraded model? we have fallback 'gpt-lite-8k' that is cheaper and lower memory.

maria: we tried auto-fallback last week but they pinned to prod model in request header. we could add a transparent hedging route: if per-tenant queue > 50 AND node util > 85% then route 20% of new requests to fallback.

chen: suggestion: implement a sliding credit pool per tenant. credit accrual tied to historical SLO-compliant usage; when credits exhausted, apply backpressure (429 or queued longer) and gradual degradation. This avoids large one-off noisy tenants from starving others.

alex: agree. also want a short-term mitigation we can enable now: throttle long-context requests at per-tenant rate-limit: "max_concurrent_long_ctx=4" + short circuit to queued fair-queue. low effort: set in admission controller config.

infra-bot: deploy triggered by alex:patch/enable-longctx-throttle to staging at 11:46 UTC — tests pass.

maria: OK let's do a controlled rollout to prod shared-us-west with 5% of traffic, watch tail latency & error rate. If safe, ramp to 50% in 10m, 100% in 30m.

leo: we should also kick off a capacity profile for acme-ads. they may need a dedicated reservation or burst token. they have consistent peak windows. Plumb a sales/contact thread for capacity conversation.

chen: long-term: prioritize implementing tenant-weighted fair-queueing in the scheduler (tokens per tenant per second, with dynamic weights based on SLA tier + historical fairness). Also expose tenant queue health in console.

alex: short-term runbook: 1) enable throttle in prod (5%) 2) monitor prom dashboards: queue_depth, p95 latency, evicted_requests 3) if backlog falls -> ramp. 4) if not -> temporary soft-eviction: reject requests over 2x baseline for that tenant with 429 + Retry-After.

maria: I'll create the on-call paging rule: if shared-us-west p95 > 1s for >5m AND eviction_rate>0.5/min -> page eng-infra.

alex: rolling the 5% throttle now. will update in 5m.

leo: one more ask — add an e2e test that simulates a noisy tenant with long context + batching so this doesn't regress.

alex: noted. thanks team.

alex: update @channel — 5% throttle rolled, after 8m the backlog dropped from 142 -> 26 and p95 fell to 230ms. keeping watch. :thumbsup:
